task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello... yes, hi. I'm having trouble with my phone. The internet on it — the mobile data — it either doesn't work at all or it's just so terribly slow. I'd really like to get it working properly, nice and fast. Can you help me with that?

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get your mobile data working properly. To start, I'll need to look up your account. Could you please provide the phone number associated with your line (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output:
User: Yes, of course. My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. 

Oh, and I should mention — I'm currently in France, visiting. I don't know if that matters, but I thought I should tell you.

turns.thought: Thank you, John. Let me look up your account now.

I've found your account and diagnosed the issue. Here's what I found for the line ending in **2002** (line L1002, Premium Plan):

**The root cause: you've used up your monthly data allowance.**
- Data used this cycle: **15.1 GB**
- Plan data limit: **15.0 GB**
- Your billing cycle ends: **2025-02-28**

When a line goes over its plan's data limit, data connectivity is cut off or severely slowed — which explains both the "doesn't work at all" and "terribly slow" symptoms you've been seeing.

A couple of other things I checked and can rule out:
- **Your line is Active** (not suspended), so cellular service itself is fine.
- **International roaming is already enabled** on your line, so being in France is not a problem — no change needed there.

**To get you back up and running at full speed, I can refuel (add) data to your line.** Your Premium Plan's refueling rate is **$2.00 per GB**, and I can add up to a maximum of **2 GB**.

How much data would you like me to add — 1 GB or 2 GB?

(Since your cycle resets on 2025-02-28, 2 GB at $4.00 would likely be enough to comfortably carry you to the reset, but the choice is yours.)
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh dear, so I've used it all up? I see... Well, I suppose that makes sense. 

Yes, let's do the 2 GB then — that's $4.00, right? I don't want to change my plan or anything, just add the data. 

But... will that definitely make it fast again? I really need it to be properly fast, not just a little bit better. I take a lot of pictures of my grandchildren and I like to send them along.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
Done — I've added **2 GB** of data to your line for **$4.00**, which will appear on your bill. Your data is restored now.

Now, about your question — **will it be *properly* fast?** Here's my honest answer: **it should be, but I can't verify it from my side**, and I want to be upfront with you about that rather than just saying "yes."

The data cutoff was a *hard stop* — nothing to do with speed. Refueling removes that stop, so you're back to your plan's normal data. Whether it's *fast* on top of that depends on your connection quality where you are, which varies with local network conditions in France.

**The best way to know for sure:** please restart your phone (power it off and back on), then test it. If your data still seems slow after a restart, tell me and I'll dig further — there are other things I can check on your device (VPN, Data Saver, network mode) that could be throttling your speed, and I'd work through those with you.

And your pictures of your grandchildren — sending those is **MMS**, which is a separate function from general mobile data. It has its own settings that can cause trouble even when data is working fine. So if photos specifically won't send after your restart, do let me know and we'll look at that separately.

Please go ahead and restart, then let me know how it's performing.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh, restart my phone? Oh my... I get nervous about that. Will I lose my pictures? I have so many photos of my grandchildren on there and I'd be absolutely devastated if anything happened to them. 

Are you quite sure it's safe?

turns.thought:
Completely understandable — and I'm very glad you asked rather than doing something you weren't comfortable with.

Here's the reassuring news: **you don't actually have to restart.** The 2 GB of data is *already applied and active* on your line — that was done on my end, and it took effect the moment I processed it. The restart isn't what makes the data work; it's just a way to prompt your phone to re-check its connection, which can help if it's still not feeling speedy.

So you have a choice:

1. **Test it now, without restarting.** Just try loading a web page or sending one of your photos. If it works well, you're all done — no restart needed at all.
2. **Restart if you want to later.** It's only ever suggested as a refresh step.

And on your real question — **no, restarting will not delete your photos.** A restart simply switches your phone's software off and back on, refreshing the running services and connections. It doesn't remove anything you've saved — not your pictures, not your messages, not your contacts. Your grandchildren are quite safe. It's a very routine action that I recommend to customers regularly, and it's the same thing that happens on its own whenever your battery runs flat and you charge it back up.

**My suggestion:** try testing your data and sending a photo right now, with no restart at all. That costs you nothing and nothing can possibly go wrong.

How does it feel? If it's still slow, or if the photos won't send, tell me and we'll take the next step together — and I'll guide you through anything that needs doing on your phone one step at a time, and never ask you to do anything that puts your pictures at risk.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, that's a relief to hear. Let me try it then... I'll check how fast it is.

turns.thought:
Please don't worry — that's genuinely useful information, and it tells me a lot.

Here's the good news: **"No Connection" is a completely different symptom from "slow."** The data cutoff I fixed would have made things slow or stop; a hard "No Connection" means your phone isn't connecting to the local network at all. So I don't think we're dealing with a data problem anymore — I think it's a **setting on your phone**, which is very fixable, and importantly, **none of these steps can touch your photos.**

Since you're in France, the most likely culprit by far is this: I've confirmed your **line** has international roaming enabled (I checked that on your account), but your **phone** also has its own separate Data Roaming switch that must be on too. Both need to be on, and the phone's one is often off by default.

**Please try this first:**

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Tap **Connections** (or on some phones, **Network & Internet** / **Mobile Networks**).
3. Look for **Data Roaming** and make sure it's switched **ON**.

While you're in there, could you also check two quick things and tell me what you see:

- **Is there an aeroplane icon (✈️) at the top of your screen?** If so, Airplane Mode is on, and that alone would cause this.
- **Do you have any signal bars at the top of the screen?** (Any at all — even just one.)

I'm afraid I can't see your phone's screen from my end, so I'm relying on your eyes here — but that's fine, we'll work through it together at your pace, one thing at a time.

Do those checks when you're ready, and tell me what you find. If Data Roaming was off, that may well be the whole fix — and turning it on costs nothing and takes effect right away.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me look at the top of my screen...

turns.thought:
Oh, this is **wonderful** news — and no, it isn't bad at all! In fact, you've just found the answer. Please stop worrying. 😊

**That aeroplane icon is Airplane Mode, and it is almost certainly the entire problem.**

Airplane Mode is a single switch that turns off *all* of your phone's wireless connections at once — mobile signal, mobile data, and Wi-Fi. That's exactly why you have no signal bars and no internet. It's not a fault, and it's not damage. And here's the important part: **it's only a switch on the software — it has absolutely nothing to do with your photos.** Your pictures are stored safely in your phone's memory and cannot be affected by this in any way.

And please don't apologise! This happens *constantly* — honestly, it's one of the most common reasons people call us. The icon is right there in the quick settings panel at the top of the screen, so a stray swipe, or a bump in your pocket or bag while travelling, can flip it on without you noticing. Nothing you did "broke" anything.

**Here's how to turn it off — the easiest way:**

1. Put your finger at the very **top of the screen** and **swipe downwards** (once, or twice if a small panel appears first).
2. You'll see a grid of little round buttons — Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, a torch, and so on.
3. Find the **aeroplane / ✈️ icon** and **tap it**. It will go from coloured/highlighted to grey, and the aeroplane symbol at the top of your screen will disappear.

*(If that panel is tricky to find, the other route is: **Settings** → **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**) → tap the **Airplane Mode** switch to off.)*

**Then:**
- Wait about **10–20 seconds** — your phone needs a moment to find the French network.
- Check the top of your screen: you should now see **signal bars** appear, and something like **4G, LTE or 5G** next to them.
- Then try loading a web page again.

Your Wi-Fi will come back on too, so if you're somewhere with hotel or café Wi-Fi, that should reconnect as well.

Take your time — there's no rush at all. Tell me what you see once you've done it: do you get signal bars and does the internet work? And if the aeroplane icon won't go away or you can't find the button, just say so and I'll walk you through it differently.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try to turn that off... I'll swipe down from the top and tap the aeroplane thing.

turns.thought:
Wonderful — you're doing brilliantly, and the aeroplane being gone plus **Excellent 5G** signal is a huge step forward! 🎉

And "Data Disabled" is **not** a problem and nothing to worry about — it's simply the very last switch in the chain, and it's the easiest one of all to fix.

Here's what's happened: Airplane Mode switched everything off, and it also turned off your **mobile data** switch. Your phone has found the network beautifully now (that's your Excellent 5G), but it's still not allowed to *use* that network for the internet until we flip this one switch.

**To turn mobile data on — the quick way:**

1. Again, swipe **down from the very top of the screen** to open that same panel of round buttons (the one where you found the aeroplane — you already know how to get there, well done).
2. Look for the button with a little **up/down arrows** symbol — it's usually labelled **Mobile Data** (it may also say "Data" or show two arrows). It's likely greyed out or crossed out right now.
3. **Tap it** so it lights up / turns coloured. The "Data Disabled" message at the top should disappear.

*(Or via menus: **Settings** → **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**) → **Mobile Networks** → tap **Mobile Data** to on.)*

**One extra thing, since you're in France:** while you're in that same panel, please also check for **Data Roaming** and make sure that's switched **on** too. Your *account* has roaming enabled — I checked that for you earlier, so you're covered there — but your *phone* has its own matching switch, and both need to be on for data to work abroad. It costs nothing to switch on.

**Then give it about 10 seconds** and try loading a web page again. I'm hoping you'll be online straight away.

And to put your mind completely at rest: **tapping these switches cannot affect your photos in any way.** You're only changing how your phone connects to the network — nothing is being deleted, moved or changed on it. Your grandchildren are safe.

Let me know how it goes — fingers crossed you'll be telling me it's working in a moment! And if you can't spot the right button or it doesn't seem to change, just describe what you see and I'll guide you from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll tap that mobile data button...

turns.thought:
Excellent — "Data Enabled" is exactly what we wanted! 🎉 And a very sharp spot on Data Saver — you've got a good eye.

**Yes, Data Saver can absolutely make things feel slow.** It deliberately reduces your data usage in the background — which means apps may not refresh until you open them, photos and messages can hang or fail to send, and web pages can feel sluggish. Since your main goal is *properly fast* data (and sending those photos), **let's turn it off.** There's no cost or downside to doing so — it's purely a restriction setting.

**To turn Data Saver off:**
1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**).
3. Tap **Data usage** (sometimes called "Data Saver" directly).
4. Tap **Data Saver** and switch it **OFF**.

*Quick alternative:* swipe down from the top of the screen again to that same panel of buttons you've been using — there may be a **Data Saver** button there (little down arrow 🔽) you can just tap off.

**And now the roaming switch on your phone:**

Good news here — **your account is already sorted.** I checked your line earlier and international roaming was already enabled, so there's nothing I need to change and nothing you'll be charged extra for. But your *phone* has its own matching switch, and both need to be on for data to work while you're in France:

1. **Settings** → **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**) → **Mobile Networks**.
2. Find **Data Roaming** and switch it **ON**.
3. If it asks "Are you sure?", confirm — it's safe, and your plan already covers it.

**Then, once both are done:**
- Give it about 10–20 seconds.
- Check the top of your screen: the "Data Saver" message should be gone, and you should still have your 5G signal.
- Try loading a web page — and then try sending one of your grandchildren's photos as a test.

Turning off Data Saver is a good idea in general, but especially for you, since **Data Saver is one of the things that can stop picture messages (MMS) from going through.** So this step is doing double duty for your photos.

And as before — none of these switches can touch your pictures. Your photos are completely safe and untouched throughout.

Let me know how the webpage and the photo go! If it's fast now and the photo sends, we're completely done. If it's still not right, tell me and we'll keep going — I won't leave you stuck.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn that Data Saver off first...

turns.thought: I'm so glad! Let me do one final check on your account to make sure nothing else is waiting that could interrupt your service.

turns.thought:
Yes — **275 Mbps and "Excellent" is the very best rating!** That's genuinely top-speed 5G, so you can stop worrying entirely. 🎉

**So, to answer you: yes, you should be able to send your photos now.** Everything that was blocking you is resolved:

- ✅ Airplane Mode — off
- ✅ Mobile Data — on (Excellent 5G, 275 Mbps)
- ✅ Data Saver — off (this was the big one for photos, as it can stop picture messages going through)
- ✅ Data Roaming — on your phone (matching your account, which was already enabled)
- ✅ Your 2 GB of extra data — applied

**Just a few notes before you go:**

**1. One thing I'd suggest trying right now, while I'm here:** send one photo as a test. Picture messages (MMS) use a slightly different setting from general internet, so it's worth confirming one goes through now rather than discovering an issue later. If it doesn't send, come straight back to me and I'll check a few MMS-specific settings with you.

**2. About your data going forward:** you'd used 15.1 GB of your 15 GB allowance, and I added 2 GB. Your billing cycle **resets on 28 February** — just three days away — so you'll get your full 15 GB back then. You're unlikely to run out before that, but if you'd like to leave Data Saver off, do — it'll keep things feeling fast.

**3. A small note on your bill:** the data refuel of 2 GB was **$4.00** (at your plan's $2.00/GB rate). It's currently on a draft bill (B1003) for the period starting 1 March, due 15 March. No action needed now — it'll just be included then. I mention it only so it isn't a surprise.

That's everything from my side. You did all the fiddly work yourself, and very calmly too — I was glad to help, and there's no need to thank me. Enjoy sending those photos of your grandchildren, and have a lovely rest of your trip in France! 🇫🇷

If anything plays up again — or you'd like that photo test checked — just ask for me anytime.
